extracted.intended_audience: examiners in International Searching and Preliminary Examining Authorities; applicants and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Official WIPO guidelines governing how International Searching Authorities and International Preliminary Examining Authorities should conduct international search and preliminary examination of PCT applications, and what applicants and practitioners may expect. Covers content requirements, search scope and strategy, report contents, examination procedure, amendments, quality framework and administrative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the description (technical field, background art, disclosure, best mode, structure and function)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must set out the technical field, background art, disclosure of the invention, brief description of drawings, best mode for carrying out the invention, structure and function, and sufficiency of disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes expectations for clarity and completeness (e.g., best mode, clear and complete disclosure), special treatment for nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings and deposit of biological material, and language requirements where references to deposited microorganisms are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure / sufficiency commensurate with the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must disclose the invention sufficiently to allow the person skilled in the art to carry it out, commensurate with the scope of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner to assess whether disclosure supports the full breadth of the claims; includes consideration of best mode, possibility of realizing special purpose, clear and complete disclosure and whether amendments introduce added subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability / utility
rubrics_metrics.description: The claimed invention must have industrial applicability (utility), meaning a practical real-world use, credible utility and, where relevant, specific/particular utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides methodology for assessing industrial applicability, types of utility (specific, substantial, credible), special purpose claims, and the date at which requirements must be met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must conform to formal requirements for form and content, including categories, independent/dependent claims, clarity, conciseness and support by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers claim categories, drafting of independent/dependent claims, interpretation principles, limitations on number/conciseness, and examples (means-plus-function, product-by-process, use claims, preamble, open/closed claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of claims (including relative terms and other terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be clear; relative terms and other ambiguous terms must be interpreted and clarified where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner is directed on interpreting unclear terms, when to object, and how lack of clarity may be expressed in written opinion or IPER; includes standardized clauses and inviting applicant to correct or amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support in description / clear and complete disclosure of claimed invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be supported by the description; there must be a clear and complete disclosure of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether claims go beyond or are inconsistent with the description; guidance on detecting added subject-matter and on recommending amendments to restore support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and acceptable number of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should be concise and the total number of claims should not be excessive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on practice regarding multiple dependent claims and conciseness; procedures where claim count or complexity affects search coverage and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of claims for search and examination purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are instructed how to interpret claims (including special formats) to determine novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes directions to adopt particular constructions to make the examiner’s conclusions understandable to designated/elected offices while noting that those offices are not bound to the interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: right to priority, determining and claiming priority dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and practice for the right to priority, how to determine priority dates and how priority claims should be made and checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner guidance on documents casting doubt on priority, correcting priority claims, and relevant dates for search and examination purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitive classification of the international application, multiple classifications and classification where scope is obscure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on classifying disclosure as filed, amended classification following published ISR, and classification when lack of unity or exclusion applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of obvious mistakes (Rule 91)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and limits for rectifying obvious mistakes in documents under Rule 91, including what mistakes cannot be rectified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers transmittal to another authority for rectification requests, invitation to applicant to request rectification, processing, authorization/effect and effective date of rectification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject matter for international search and preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain subject matter is excluded from search/examination: scientific/mathematical theories, plant/animal varieties or essentially biological processes (other than microbiological), schemes/rules/methods of doing business or purely mental acts, surgical/therapeutic treatment and diagnostic methods practiced on the human or animal body, mere presentations of information, and computer programs to the extent Authority is not equipped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General considerations for assessing subject-matter nature, treatment of forms of claims, cases of doubt, examples when search/examination is possible or not, and special appendices on schemes/business methods and computer programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of search and preliminary examination in special situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how far the search and examination should extend in particular situations (e.g., unclear claims, excluded matter, non-prior-art issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes examples where a search is possible with indication in the written opinion, exceptional situations where no search is possible, and handling cases like perpetual motion, sequence listings, and non-written disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention determination
rubrics_metrics.description: How to determine whether unity of invention exists (single general inventive concept) and handling of multiple inventions in one application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive illustrations (examples 1–43) for combinations of claim categories, Markush practice, intermediate/final products, complementary forms, alternative forms, dependent claims diverging from inventive concept; procedures for invitations to pay additional fees, search of additional inventions, protests, and a posteriori lack of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art: what constitutes prior art and relevant dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and methodology for identifying prior art, relevant dates for ISR and written opinion/IPER purposes, and documents that may cast doubt on priority claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses documents not within prior art that may still be relevant, later published patent applications, availability and reliability of internet disclosures, establishing dates, and relating dates to individual claims or parts of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty assessment (meaning and methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for assessing novelty, including inherent/implicit disclosure, interpretation of claims, combining documents, generic vs specific disclosures and ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner methodology and examples on determining novelty and dealing with issues like inherent disclosure and combining teachings from multiple sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step / non-obviousness assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and considerations for determining inventive step: what is 'obvious', the person skilled in the art, combining teachings, assessing contribution against prior art and problem-solution approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discussion of ex post facto analysis, technical value, long-felt need, commercial success, treatment of dependent claims, examples and appendices on problem-solution approach and single-document situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing industrial applicability during search/examination
rubrics_metrics.description: How to judge whether the invention is industrially applicable including methodologies and examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers special considerations for utility claims (specific, substantial, credible), dates for requirement satisfaction, and when lack of industrial applicability should be raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective and scope of the international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective is to identify relevant earlier disclosures; scope includes minimum documentation and possibly more depending on the claims and field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on examiner responsibilities, basis of the search, orientation and subject of search, analysis of claims, treatment of inventions for which no fees paid, full coverage vs speculative claims and dependent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy (preliminary steps, field of search, databases, conducting search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should follow a search strategy including preliminary steps (classification, abstract/title review), determining field of search, analogous fields, choice of documentation/databases, and conducting/stopping/recording the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes security considerations for internet searching, what to do if no documents found, how to record the search and when to stop (e.g., diminishing returns, lack of meaningful search possibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and citation of prior art in ISR (identifying most relevant portions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for selecting citations and indicating the most relevant portions of cited documents in the International Search Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on citation categories (particularly relevant documents, documents defining state of the art, intermediate documents, documents relating to theory/principle, potentially conflicting patent docs), relationship between documents and claims, and marking of quotations or relevant passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and form of the International Search Report (ISR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for preparing the ISR: time limits, form and language, what to include on the form (PCT/ISA/210) and associated notification (PCT/ISA/220).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details on completing fields like earliest priority date, total number of sheets, indication of whether copies of cited prior art are attached, handling cases where no or limited report is established, and filling of the notification of transmittal and written opinion forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of the ISR and treatment of special disclosures (sequence listings, non-written disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the basis of the ISR including handling nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings, references to main ISR, restriction of search subject, and treatment of non-written disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on fields searched, minimum documentation searched, electronic databases consulted, previous searches, and how to cite documents that refer to non-written disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary international search procedure and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for requesting and conducting supplementary international searches, their basis, and which claims may be excluded from supplementary search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers requesting supplementary searches, start and withdrawal of request, basis of supplementary search (e.g., language/geographical coverage), claims excluded from supplementary search, and filing/copy transmission practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of written opinions and International Preliminary Examination Report (IPER)
rubrics_metrics.description: What must be included in written opinions and IPERs (overview of content, boxes I–VIII covering basis, priority, non-establishment, lack of unity, reasoned statements, cited documents, defects and observations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed guidance on language considerations, treatment of amendments (gaps in numbering, going beyond original disclosure), top-up searches, rectification of mistakes, standardized clauses, ensuring utility for later stages, and finalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with major objections first in written opinions/IPER
rubrics_metrics.description: When issuing opinions/reports, major objections (e.g., excluded subject matter, lack of unity, lack of novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability) should be addressed first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes separate treatment where no international search was made for some or all claims, how to structure the report and use standard clauses to make the report maximally useful for national/regional phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to correct or amend and handling applicant responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for inviting applicants to correct defects or file amendments and how responses are to be handled during international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes minimum time limits for invitations (not less than 10 days nor more than one month), requirements for documents (cover letters, language), translations of amendments, and consequences of failing to provide translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure before the International Preliminary Examining Authority (demand filing and time limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for filing a demand for international preliminary examination, checking and notifying receipt, commencement, stages of examination, top-up searches, and applicable time limits for completing examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on first and further stages of examination, cases where no written opinion is required, correction of IPER, and determination of time limits and failure consequences if applicant does not respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making and appraising amendments (Article 19 and Article 34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and appraisal standards for amendments under Article 19 (after ISR) and Article 34 (during examination), including appraisal of added subject-matter, lack of support and translated applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers amendments prior to start of IPER, appraisal of amendments for added subject-matter/new matter, lack of support, handling of translations and rectification of obvious mistakes; Appendix on new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence listings furnished for search/examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for sequence listings furnished specifically for international search or preliminary examination which do not form part of the application as filed, and how they are handled, labelled and transmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If furnished online, encode purpose and application number in filename/metadata; physical media labeled 'SUBSEQUENTLY FURNISHED SEQUENCE LISTING NOT FORMING PART OF THE INTERNATIONAL APPLICATION'; Authority transmits copy to International Bureau and may collect fees for additional copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of ISR, written opinion, IPER and related documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities must transmit required reports and annexes to the International Bureau and applicant, place copies in examination files and notify when Article 34 amendments were not taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific forms and same-day obligations (e.g., use of Forms PCT/IPEA/415, PCT/IPEA/416), and International Bureau’s role in communicating documents to elected/elected Offices and public availability after expiry of 30 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for excuse of delay and extension of time limits (Rule 82quater)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which delay in meeting time limits is excused (war, strike, natural calamity, epidemic, general unavailability of electronic communications, etc.), evidence requirements, and authority powers to waive evidence or establish extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details on acceptable evidence (news reports, statements from providers), criteria for 'as soon as reasonably possible', Rule 82quater.2 option to excuse delays due to Authority electronic unavailability, Rule 82quater.3 for Authority-established extension periods (max two months, may be renewed) and publication/notification obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time limits and related procedural computations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to computation of time limits (Rule 80) and guidance for determining dates of documents and expiry of time limits, especially when extensions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes how periods established under Rule 82quater.3 affect expiry dates and that priority period is unaffected since it is not a Regulation-fixed time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical and administrative procedures for demands and file management
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for receipt of demands, determination and marking of competent authority, identification of international application, entitlement to file a demand, change in applicant, election of States, checks affecting date of receipt and timeliness, establishing Authority file and transmittal to International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on handling certain defects (language, signature, applicant/agent indications), invitations to correct defects, payment/refund of fees, transfer of handling fees, use of facsimile/telecommunications, handling paper submissions in electronic-workflow Authorities, irregularities in mail service, and processing of sequence listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality framework for international search and preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Common quality framework comprising leadership/policy, risk-based practices, resources, workload management, quality assurance, communication, documentation, search process documentation, internal review and reporting arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies resource expectations (sufficient human, material, training resources and oversight), inter-authority communication, guidance to users, communication with WIPO/designated and elected Offices, and future development considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling cases where no meaningful search is possible or declaration of non-establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on situations where a meaningful search cannot be carried out for all or some claims and procedures for declaring non-establishment of an ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include excluded subject matter, unclear claims, perpetual motion, or where Authority lacks equipment (e.g., computer program search). Includes how to record and communicate such non-establishment in Box III of written opinion/IPER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized clauses and structuring reports to maximize usefulness for later stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports and opinions should use standardized clauses and be structured so as to be of maximal use to national/regional Offices and the applicant during later stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes use of Boxes I–VIII, stating the basis of objections, recommending amendments, and providing reasoned statements to assist designated/elected Offices even though they are not bound by the Authority’s conclusions.
